 Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.13,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 24-01-2020, at 09:45 P.M., the petitioner was pedestrian walking on the left side of the road carefully, cautiously, slowly, observing all traffic rules, proceeding on S.D.
Road, Sacredheart College, near B.E.M.C. Junction.
At that time, the motorcycle bearing No. KA-03-JK-4606 ridden by its rider in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to St. John's Medical College Hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein she took further treatment as an indoor patient.

sentences.text: Earlier to the accident, she was working as Aya (Servant) at Shishugraha School and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she became permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Indiranagar Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.13,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 appeared through their respective counsels and filed their separate written statements.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-JK-4606 in favour of respondent No.2 and the same was valid as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Section 149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has further contended that the rider of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence to ride the same.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the age, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by the petitioner.
It has contended that, there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle in issue as he was proceeding with due care and cautious by following the traffic rules and regulations.

On the contrary, the alleged accident was due to the sole negligence of the petitioner who was pedestrian crossing he road in negligent manner without following the traffic rules and regulations and caused the accident.
It has contended that the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It is further contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exaggerated.
In view of above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.
5. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
He has contended that, the rider of the bicycle in question was having valid driving licence at the time of accident.
He has denied the age, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by the petitioner.
He has further contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exaggerated.

He has further contended that the said vehicle has been duly insured with respondent No.1 and insurance policy was in force as on the date of accident and in case of any compensation has to be awarded by this Hon'ble Tribunal, the liability shall be on the respondent No.1.
In view of above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 24-01-2020, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-03-JK- 4606 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
7.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has got examined himself as R.W.1.
No document has been got marked by the respondent No.2.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.

9. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Partly Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 24-01-2020, at 09:45 P.M., the petitioner was pedestrian walking on the left side of the road carefully, cautiously, slowly, observing all traffic rules, proceeding on S.D. Road, Sacredheart College, near B.E.M.C. Junction.
At that time, the motorcycle bearing No. KA-03-JK-4606 ridden by its rider in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, she was doing agriculture and milk vending and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has became permanently disabled and has lost her earning capacity.
11. In order to prove her case, the petitioner has examined herself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein she has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of her oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 33 documents as Ex.P.1 to 33.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of FIR, Ex.P.2 is true copy of First Information Statement, Ex.P.3 is Sketch, Ex.P.4 is Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.5 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.6 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.7 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.8 is true copy of notice under Sec.133 of M.V. Act, Ex.P.9 is true copy of reply to said notice, Ex.P.10 is Discharge summary, Ex.P.11 is Radiology report, Ex.P.12 is Medical bills (total 58), Ex.P.13 is Estimation,

Ex.P.14 is Letter issued by Shishu Griha School, Ex.P.15 are Salary slips (total 3), Ex.P.16 are Prescriptions (total 11), Ex.P.17 is Advance receipts (total 4), Ex.P.18 are Photos and C.D., Ex.P.19 is M.L.C extract, Ex.P.20 is OPD sheet, Ex.P.21 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.22 is Disability Calculation Certificate, Ex.P.23 to 25 are In-patient records (total 3), Ex.P.26 is X-ray, Ex.P.27 is Service Certificate, Ex.P.28 is Attested copy of Resignation Letter, Ex.P.29 to 31 are Pay slips (total 3), Ex.P.32 is Salary Receipt and Ex.P.33 is Resignation Letter.
12. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, the date, time and place of accident, involvement of offending vehicle, issuance of insurance policy and its validity are not in dispute.

Further, though,
the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the said facts in its written statement, they have not produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Even the respondent No.1 has not stepped into witness box to depose the contentions taken in its written statement on oath.

13. sentences.text: At that time, the motorcycle bearing No. KA-03-JK-4606 ridden by its rider in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.

The investigation officer in his final report has clearly stated that, on the alleged date, time and place of accident, due to rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-03-JK-4606 the said accident has taken place.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.1 has clearly admitted in her cross-examination that, the said accident has taken place while she was crossing the road at Jagadeesh Nagar, the said road being a State Highway is busy traffic road.
Further, she has clearly admitted that, the said accident has taken place at the middle of the road and before accident she had seen the offending motorcycle from far distance proceeding towards her.

But, the petitioner/P.W.1, has unequivocally denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 that, the said accident is caused to her own negligence and there was no negligence on the part of driver of offending motorcycle.
This clearly goes to show that, there was some contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner also.

Further, the Ex.P.3 spot sketch and Ex.P.4 spot mahazer, also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place at the middle of 40 feet width two way State Highway, while the petitioner was crossing the road as a pedestrian.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.10 discharge summaries, Ex.P.11 radiology report, Ex.P.23 to 25 inpatient records and Ex.P26 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and she has suffered left shaft of humerus fracture (closed) with (L) 4th metacarpal fracture - open.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 insurance company has not led any rebuttal evidence to show that, the petitioner has not suffered the above injuries.
Further, the respondent No.1 insurance company has not adduced any evidence to substantiate the contentions taken in its written statement.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-03-JK-4606.
15.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, no where in the police records or even in the evidence of P.W.1, it is stated that, at the place of accident there were pedestrian crossing mark or zebra mark to cross the road.

If the petitioner after seeing the offending motorcycle proceeding towards her had waited for a while and not attempted to cross the road till passing of the said motorcycle, the said accident would not have caused.

The oral and documentary evidence on record clearly goes to show that, the attempt made by the petitioner while trying to cross the road from the place where she was not permitted to cross, resulted in accident and she has sustained grievous injuries.
16. Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.7, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there is no other vehicle involved in the accident, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to some negligence of the rider of offending vehicle.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross- examination of P.W.1 to show that, there was absolutely no fault or negligence on the part of rider of offending motorcycle.

17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

Road,
Sacredheart College, near B.E.M.C. Junction, Bengaluru.
But, failed to prove that, the said accident has occurred due to the sole rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
There is equal contributory negligence on the part of petitioner and on the part of rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-JK-4606.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of motorcycle bearing KA-03- JK-4606 and she has sustained fracture of tibia and fibula of her left leg and for the said injuries she has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport,
actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.,

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the discharge summary, which is marked as Ex.P.10.
As per Ex.P.10, the age of the petitioner is 53 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered left shaft of humerus fracture (closed) with (L) 4th metacarpal fracture - open and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgery i.e. debridement and open reduction internal fixation + DCP for left humerus and closed reduction internal fixation for metacarpal injury.
Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered 18.9% physical disability for the whole body.
The oral evidence of P.W.2 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.
The Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.10 discharge summaries, Ex.P.11 radiology report, Ex.P.23 to 25 in-patient records and Ex.P26 x-ray

, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and she has suffered left shaft of humerus fracture (closed) with (L) 4th metacarpal fracture - open.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made in to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 24-01-2020 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 25-07-2023, which is after lapse of three years and four months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the the petitioner requires plastic surgery correction for hand deformity.
Further, the petitioner has also deposed in his examination- in-chief affidavit that, he is still continuing follow up treatment.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the fractures of the petitioner are completely united and implants are removed.

Further, he has clearly admitted that, in the discharge summary given on second time, there is no mention of any complications and problem regarding the process of healing of the fracture and physiotherapy is the best mode of treatment for avoiding restrictions of range of movement of joints.
Further, he has clearly admitted that, the petitioner has been advised for physiotherapy and he has continued the treatment of physiotherapy.

Therefore, in such circumstances, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.

a) The petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, before accident she was working as Aya (Servant)
at Shishugraha School and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.

Further, she has deposed that,
due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident she is unable to do Aya work.

In this regard she has produced letter issued by Sishu Griha School, salary slips (total 3), salary certificate, resignation letter, pay slips (total 3), salary receipt and resignation letter as per Ex.P.14, 15 and 27 to 33.
Further, she has also examined Administration Office Staff at Sishu Griha School as PW3.

From these documents, it is clear that, the Rani.D vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83421432/

The school has accepted her resignation and since then she has not been paid salary.

b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 53 years is 11.

ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, she has produced 58 medical bills, as per Ex.P.12.

But,
the petitioner/P.W.1 has clearly admitted in her cross- examination that, the said medical bills have been paid by the insurance company and she has not produced any document to show that, how much amount she has paid towards medical expenses.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation under the head of medical expenses to the petitioner does not arise.
Hence, no compensation has been awarded under the head medical expenses.

iii) Pain and sufferings: In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on her left hand i.e. suffered left shaft of humerus fracture (closed) with (L) 4th metacarpal fracture - open.

As per Ex.P.10 discharge summaries and Ex.P.23 to 25 inpatient records (total 3), the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 24 days from 25-01-2020 to 12-02-2020 and 11-10-2022 to 15-10-2022, in St. Johns Medical College Hospital, Bengaluru.

viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 53 years and unfortunately she has suffered fracture of weight bearing bones i.e. left shaft of humerus fracture (closed) with (L) 4th metacarpal fracture - open.
The evidence shows that, she has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 12% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner requires plastic surgery correction for hand deformity.
But, no estimation has been provided by him.

Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/-

21. While answering Issue No.1 this court has already come to conclusion that there is equal contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner and the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-JK-4606.

Accordingly, it is held that the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 3,69,072-00 2.
Medical expenses Nil 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4.

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,70,436/-
with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
22. Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-03-JK-4606 the accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,70,436/- from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
23. ISSUE No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.13,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
At that time, the motorcycle bearing No. KA-03-JK-4606 ridden by its rider in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.
Earlier to the accident, she was working as Aya (Servant) at Shishugraha School and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she became permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Indiranagar Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
